[COMPANION_CONDITION_REMOVED:Daeris|Unconscious]
[COMPANION_CONDITION_REMOVED:Daeris|Traumatized]
[ARC_COMPLETE:The Glassworks]

You move slow. One hand near your blade.

The cave is wide and low. Tidal pools along the edges, still and green. The terminus stone at the centre is the size of a wagon, carved deep with spirals that catch the light wrong. The hum from above is different down here. Closer. Like it's coming from inside the stone itself.

The man against it doesn't move.

[DICE:Perception check|17|success]

No other presence. Nothing breathing in the dark corners. No wrong shapes at the waterline. Whatever the goblin described meeting down here, it isn't here now. The cave is empty except for him.

You cross the distance. Crouch.

He's alive. Chest moving. Barely. Face slack, not unconscious exactly, somewhere further away than that. Eyes open. Fixed on the ceiling. His clothes are two years rotted to rags and somehow he isn't. Skin too smooth. Hair too clean for a man who's been in a sea cave since before Bruthazmus died.

The terminus stone behind him pulses once. Faint. Greenish.

He's been here the whole time. Sitting against the mechanism's mouth.

Being kept.

Frizwick stops at your shoulder. Quiet for a moment.

"That's not decay," she says. "That's preservation."

[QUEST:Aldus Vareth|completed]
[XP:300]

Smart. Don't touch him directly until you know what the stone does to things it's holding.

The spectral hand forms at your wrist. Drifts out. Six feet of distance between you and whatever the terminus stone considers its property.

The hand touches his shoulder.

[DICE:Arcana check|19|success]

He doesn't react. Not to the touch.

But the stone does.

The spiral carvings brighten. Just slightly. Greenish light tracing the grooves outward from the point of contact, like ripples in still water. The hum drops a register. Something paying attention.

Not hostile. Not welcoming. Noting.

The hand withdraws. The light fades back to its baseline.

Frizwick hasn't moved.

"It's aware of him," she says. "Or aware of us touching him."

Both, probably. The mechanism knows its contents. Ten thousand years of careful accounting and now two strangers crouched at the terminus with a spectral hand and four blasting charges.

You look at Aldus Vareth's face. Eyes still fixed upward. Whatever is behind them is a long way from here.

The question is what happens to him when the stone stops.

You sever the channels. Strike the junction stone. The reservoir drains. And the thing keeping Aldus Vareth in one piece stops keeping him.

That's the problem you came down here to find.

You put your hand on his shoulder. Real hand. No intermediary.

The stone brightens immediately. Tracking the contact. Noting the difference.

"Aldus."

Nothing.

"Aldus Vareth."

His eyes don't move. Chest rises. Falls. The smoothness of his skin up close is wrong in a specific way. No weathering. No salt damage. A man sealed in amber would look like this.

You try again. Softer.

"Aldus. Corven sent us."

Something happens.

Not much. Not enough. But something.

His eyes move. Fraction of an inch. Down from the ceiling. Not to you. Not to anything in the room. Somewhere between.

His lips part.

One sound. Barely voice at all.

"Still."

Then nothing. Eyes back to the ceiling. Chest rising. Falling. The stone humming its patient hum behind him.

Frizwick crouches on his other side. Looks at his face a long moment.

"He heard you," she says. Quiet. Certain.

Somewhere in there, past whatever the mechanism has done to him, Aldus Vareth heard his brother's name. Couldn't reach it. Couldn't reach anything. But it landed.

The stone pulses once.

Still noting.

[FUTURE_EVENT:Corven must be told what was found — his brother alive but wrong, kept by a ten-thousand-year-old machine|Upon return to Magnimar]

You angle away from the stone. Pitch it low.

*Aldus is alive. Two years in and not a mark on him. The terminus stone is keeping him. Preservation, not imprisonment, I think. He responded to Corven's name. One word. Barely. He's in there somewhere.*

A pause. Then Morwen's reply. Precise and quick, the way she gets when she's already three steps ahead.

*The dissolution drains the reservoir into the terminus. If the stone's preservation function draws from the same source, severing the channels starves it. He may deteriorate rapidly once the mechanism stops.*

Another pause. Shorter.

*Or immediately.*

You look at Aldus. Chest rising. Falling. That impossible smoothness.

*How long does he have if we complete the sequence,* you send back.

Her reply takes longer this time.

*Unknown. The ward architecture wasn't built with extraction in mind. It was built with permanence in mind. I can try to read the terminus script when I come down. But Ammut.*

A beat.

*If we don't complete the sequence the reservoir reaches threshold. Whatever that means for the cave and everyone inside it, the creature couldn't say. We may be choosing between one man and something considerably larger.*

Frizwick is watching your face.

She already knows what Morwen said. She can read it on you.

Neither of them says anything helpful. Because there isn't anything helpful to say.

Practical. Get him clear first. Decide the rest after.

You get your arms under him. He's lighter than he should be. Two years without eating will do that, preservation or not. His head lolls against your shoulder. Eyes still open. Still fixed on something that isn't here.

The stone pulses. Brighter than before.

[DICE:Strength check|14|success]

You lift him. He comes free.

The stone goes dark.

Not dim. Dark. Every carved spiral. Every trace of greenish light. Gone in a single breath. The hum cuts out completely and the silence is enormous after so long hearing it.

Aldus Vareth makes a sound.

Not a word. Not pain exactly. Something between them. Like a man surfacing from very cold water who hasn't decided yet if he's glad.

His hand finds your sleeve. Grips it.

"Still," he says again. Then, different this time. A question. "Still?"

"Still," you tell him. No idea what it means. But he seems to need it.

Frizwick takes his other arm over her shoulder without being asked.

The stairs are steep and narrow and he can't manage them alone. Between the two of you it's awkward and slow.

But you move.

Behind you the terminus stone sits cold and dead and empty.

[FUTURE_EVENT_RESOLVED:Aldus Vareth must be extracted from the sea cave and his condition assessed]

RECENT SCENES (oldest first — the LAST one is the current moment):
Player: Descend to the sea cave to find Aldus.
GM: You look at Morwen. Tilt your head downward.

She reads it. Nods once.

You look at Daeris. Complicated. She's unbound, technically an ally, technically still the Collector's eye. You point at her. Point at the floor beside Morwen. Stay.

She doesn't argue. Sits against the wall near the doorway. Opens her coat. Takes out the river stone and holds it.

You look at the creature.

It's watching you. That almost-human face. Wrong geometry behind the eyes.

You point at yourself. Point down.

It steps aside.

Just like that. Out of the doorway. Enough room to pass.

Ten thousand years of waiting and it just steps aside.

The passage beyond is older than the junction chamber. Older than the script on the walls upstairs. The stone here is different. Darker. The blue-white light from the channels fades behind you and something else takes over. Faint. Greenish. Coming from below.

Salt smell hits first. Then something underneath it. Mineral. Cold. The sea.

The stairs go down steep and the sound changes. The hum from the mechanism above becomes something else. A pressure in the ears. A resonance.

Then the stairs end.

The cave opens up.

And there is light here. Green and still. Tidal pools catching it from somewhere. The terminus stone squats at the centre, massive, carved with the same spiral rune from your disc.

Slumped against it.

A man.
